sentences.text: Initially, scientists thought Enaliornis was a loon or diver because it lacked specific traits found in other members of its group.
Evidence suggests the bird possessed wings that were poorly developed for flight.
The largest species, Enaliornis barretti, reached a size comparable to a large pigeon.
It remains undetermined whether this ancient bird had teeth, unlike other members of its order.
Unlike modern water birds, Enaliornis likely possessed lobed feet adapted for swimming instead of webbed feet.
Three distinct species have been described, ranging from the small E. sedgwicki to the large E. barretti.
The genus was first described by Harry Seeley in 1876.
Seeley originally named the genus Pelagornis in 1866, but the name had to be changed because it was already used for a Miocene bird.
Fossils of Enaliornis have been discovered near Cambridge, England.
Enaliornis belongs to the parent group Hesperornithiformes.
Enaliornis lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
